item.title: The Mayor of a City in Haiti Warned of a Massacre. No One Listened.
item.description: The mayor of Kenscoff, a town near Haiti’s capital, wrote government officials hundreds of letters to warn of gang threats. Then dozens of people died, and he did, too.

item.title: Hegseth Said to Make Unannounced Visit to Israel for Talks With Netanyahu
item.description: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth met with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Israel’s defense minister, a week before a pivotal election.

item.title: The A.I. Data Center Backlash Has Reached a Quiet Corner of Rural England
item.description: Plans to build one of Europe’s largest data centers in Devon have been met by strong opposition from residents, as environmental concerns grow.

item.title: Australian Lawmaker Helen Haines Remains in Critical Condition After Car Attack
item.description: Helen Haines, an independent, remained in critical condition after she was struck by a vehicle. A 43-year-old man was charged and will appear in court on Wednesday.

item.title: As Alberta Rejects Canada Separatism, Carney Gets Much of the Credit
item.description: Prime Minister Mark Carney won over Canada’s most conservative province by promising a pipeline and campaigning hard, defeating its efforts to secede.
